subject: Rule-based fallback exemption and demo handoff
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Alex Patel <alex@brightlane.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rule-based fallback exemption and demo handoff

Hi team,

Quick context: BrightLane is in ramp and has a scheduled executive demo with their CTO next Tuesday. During today's POC they hit a class of requests where our standard variant fallback (cost-first routing) is producing degraded latency for short, latency-sensitive prompts. The customer wants a temporary override so the demo uses a low-latency variant (higher cost) for requests matching a simple rule (prompt metadata header `x-brightlane-critical: true`).

Ask: can Platform/Runtime provide a short-lived "rule-based fallback exemption" that: 1) routes requests with that header to the low-latency variant bypassing cost-tier fallback, 2) can be toggled at the project level, and 3) is scoped to BrightLane for the demo window (1 week)? We need an ETA and risk assessment — if a full config change is heavy, is there a faster canary-level approach?

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_brightlane.pdf (MAP) and a short sample trace (sample_trace_20290314.txt) that shows the failing requests.

Customer ask is time-boxed: demo on 2029-03-19 (next Tue). If we can't do a config-level exemption, they'd like a documented workaround for SalesEng to execute before demo.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Alex Patel <alex@brightlane.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2029 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rule-based fallback exemption and demo handoff

Marissa — thanks for the clear write-up and trace. A few clarifying Qs up front:

- Volume/ratio: approximately how many of their requests match this header today and what QPS do you expect during the demo (ballpark)?
- Is the header added by BrightLane on the client side, or is it derived by their proxy? If client-set, an allowlist is easier.

Technical note: our current smart-routing evaluates cost vs latency at request time and can fall back across variants by model family. Exempting by rule would require either (A) a routing exception table keyed by customer+header evaluated at the routing layer, or (B) a temporary per-project tag that forces the routing decision to prefer latency variants. Option A is more surgical but requires a small runtime change to read the header at routing time; Option B can be faked by setting a project-level override flag but risks broader exposure if the flag isn't scoped tightly.

If Sales needs a short-term play, we can do a controlled project-tag override that Logan and I can monitor — but I want to flag two risks: cold-cache costs for the latency variants and potential capacity contention if multiple customers request similar overrides.

I can do a quick spike today to estimate code + deploy effort for the routing exception table.

—Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Alex Patel <alex@brightlane.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2029 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rule-based fallback exemption and demo handoff

Karthik, Marissa — quick additions from Serving/Capacity side:

- We need the expected QPS and percent critical (see Karthik's question). If it's > 25 QPS sustained we need to reserve capacity on the low-latency pool or performance will suffer.
- Sample payloads are helpful to check sequence length distribution; very short prompts are where latency variance is highest. The sample_trace helps but if you can include a small set of raw JSON requests that would be ideal.
- Operationally I can expose a temporary project-level tag for BrightLane that forces variant preference for the demo window. This is the fastest path. Steps: 1) create tag+policy, 2) add automatic rollback at end of window, 3) monitor token-cost and latency metrics.

If we take the tag approach, we'll want SalesEng (Marissa) to own enabling/disabling and an SRE to watch metrics during the demo. If they want the more surgical header-based exception, Karthik's approach is better but likely a 3-5 day turnaround (spike + PR + canary).

—Logan
Director, Serving Runtime
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Alex Patel <alex@brightlane.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2029 13:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rule-based fallback exemption and demo handoff

On Fri, Mar 15, 2029 at 11:18 AM Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> If we take the tag approach, we'll want SalesEng (Marissa) to own enabling/disabling and an SRE to watch metrics during the demo. If they want the more surgical header-based exception, Karthik's approach is better but likely a 3-5 day turnaround (spike + PR + canary).

Agree with Logan. A few implementation details from Console/Control Plane:

- We can introduce a temporary "route:prefer-low-latency" project tag that the control plane will include in the routing decision context. This avoids touching core routing code in the short term and keeps the change confined to project metadata + routing policy evaluation.
- I'll draft the rollout steps: create tag in Control Plane UI, add policy mapping in routing config (non-destructive), create a time-bound policy TTL, run a canary for 30 minutes on dev and then schedule a production window.
- Caveat: tags are evaluated at request time; if BrightLane is on an older SDK that doesn't forward project metadata, SalesEng will need to set the tag server-side or we default to request-header approach.

I'll prepare a short runbook for Marissa with precise clicks/flags and a monitoring checklist (latency p50/p95, error rate, token spend delta). Can do that by EOD.

—Stephanie
Product Manager, Control Plane
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Alex Patel <alex@brightlane.ai>, BrightLane Procurement <procurement@brightlane.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2029 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rule-based fallback exemption and demo handoff

Thanks all — this is super helpful and pragmatic. Plan I'm pulling together for the customer:

1) Short-term (fast path, for demo): Stephanie will create the project-level tag "route:prefer-low-latency" and provide the runbook. Sales will enable the tag for the BrightLane project Friday evening and disable it after the demo window. Logan + SRE will monitor during the demo.
2) Medium-term (if customer wants this permanently): Karthik will spike the header-based routing exception table to evaluate 3-5 day implementation cost and safety controls (allowlist, audit logging).
3) Offer: Sergio, propose we pitch BrightLane a 2-week pilot with default capacity reservation and a small trial credit to offset cost delta — this will soften procurement asks.

Deliverables & owners:
- Runbook + control-plane steps: Stephanie (EOD)
- Tag creation + temporary enablement: Logan (today)
- Spike for header-based exception: Karthik (start Mon, 3/18)
- Customer comms & pilot offer: Sergio + Marissa

Alex — will loop you separately with exact steps and a short checklist for your CTO demo.

If there are any blockers to the quick tag approach please flag them now.

—Marissa
